questions.prompt: Two events $A$ and $B$ are such that $P(B) = 0.60$ and $P(A \cap B) = 0.15$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find $P(A \mid B)$.

questions.prompt: A music school records each student's instrument. Out of $100$ students, $30$ play drums. Among the $30$ drum players, $12$ are male and $18$ are female.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: A student is chosen at random. Given that the student plays drums, find the probability that the student is male.

questions.prompt: Two fair four-sided dice, each labelled $1, 2, 3, 4$, are rolled together.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Given that at least one die shows a $2$, find the probability that the sum of the scores is $6$.

questions.prompt: Two events $A$ and $B$ satisfy $P(B) = 0.40$ and $P(A \cap B') = 0.18$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find $P(A \mid B')$.

questions.prompt: A fair spinner labelled $1, 2, 3$ is spun twice.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Given that the first score is odd, find the probability that the product of the two scores is at most $3$.

questions.prompt: For two events $A$ and $B$, $P(B) = 0.75$ and $P(A \cap B) = 0.45$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the value of $P(A \mid B)$ in simplest decimal or fractional form.

questions.prompt:
The table below categorises $150$ students in a creative arts academy by age division and elective course:

$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|}\hline & \text{Drama} & \text{Music} & \text{Art} \\\hline \text{Junior} & 20 & 45 & 15 \\\hline \text{Senior} & 10 & 30 & 30 \\\hline\end{array}$$

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly chosen student takes Art, given that the student is a Senior.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly chosen student is a Junior, given that the student takes Music.

questions.prompt: Two fair standard six-sided dice, each numbered $1$ to $6$, are rolled simultaneously.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Given that the first die shows a $3$, find the probability that the sum of the two dice is odd.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given that the sum of the two dice is $8$, find the probability that the first die shows a prime number.

questions.prompt: An employee travels to work by bus with probability $0.60$ and by train with probability $0.40$. When travelling by bus, the probability of being late is $0.05$. When travelling by train, the probability of being late is $0.15$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the overall probability that the employee is late for work.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given that the employee arrives late for work, find the probability that the employee travelled by train.

questions.prompt: Refer to the commuter scenario from the previous question: an employee travels by bus with probability $0.60$ (late with probability $0.05$) and by train with probability $0.40$ (late with probability $0.15$).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the probability that the employee is not late for work.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given that the employee is not late for work, find the probability that the employee travelled by bus.

questions.prompt: A manufacturing plant produces components using three machines: $A$, $B$, and $C$. Machine $A$ produces $50\%$ of the total output, Machine $B$ produces $30\%$, and Machine $C$ produces $20\%$. The defect rates for the components produced by Machines $A$, $B$, and $C$ are $2\%$, $3\%$, and $5\%$ respectively.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: A component is selected at random from the plant's production. Find the probability that the component is defective.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given that the selected component is found to be defective, find the probability that it was manufactured by Machine $B$.

questions.prompt: A pouch contains $5$ red marbles and $4$ white marbles. Two marbles are selected at random from the pouch without replacement.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the probability that at least one of the selected marbles is red.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the probability that both selected marbles are red.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Given that at least one of the selected marbles is red, find the probability that both selected marbles are red.

questions.prompt: A box contains $4$ red balls, $3$ green balls, and $2$ blue balls. Three balls are drawn successively at random from the box without replacement.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the probability that at least two of the three balls drawn are red.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given that at least two of the balls drawn are red, find the probability that all three balls drawn are red.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Given that at least two of the balls drawn are red, find the probability that the third ball drawn is green.
